prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, building on earlier tin-amide precedent, through ligand design grounded in the mechanism of the catalytic cycle

statement.case_for: After the first round I still prefer B035 with Buchwald and Hartwig as a single part. The chair's summary shows that no configuration has more than two explicit supporters, so I weigh which candidacy can be stated most precisely and verified most easily. This one can. Five members ranked it in the opening and every member who proposed names chose the same pair. The scientific content is a mechanism-led achievement: bulky biaryl monophosphines and chelating bisphosphines made oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination work for a broad range of amines, and the rate-limiting steps were identified and then engineered around. That is the kind of physical-organic understanding made practical that I value. Three decades of independent use leave no maturity question. The 2010 prize cited C-C coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki), so a C-N citation is a distinct achievement. I have written the citation so that it acknowledges the tin-amide precedent and does not claim the first palladium-mediated C-N bond formation, which answers the priority concern directly.
statement.case_against: The main weakness is still the one I raised and Somfai and Aqvist also noted: B035 is a method, and it follows a recent prize in the same catalytic family. Kosugi's tin-amide work is a genuine precursor, and the three-name cap means I cannot treat it as a footnote unless the expert report shows it was neither catalytic in a general sense nor mechanistically developed. Somfai himself concedes the concept is less novel than B010 or B011. I also cannot judge organometallic priority from my own field and rely on the report on this point. Finally, B010 has the broadest support as an alternative, and if the committee cannot move beyond two supporters per configuration, my attachment to B035 should not block a candidacy that more members find acceptable, provided its citation can be made accurate.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B035 with the same pair and says Kosugi's tin-amide precedent must be stated carefully in the citation. He also accepts that it may struggle for a majority against candidacies with broader reach.
responses.response: We agree on the pair, and I have now put the Kosugi precedent into the citation text so it is not misrepresented. I am not persuaded that the weaker conceptual novelty is a defect we should accept without comment. The achievement here is the ligand-controlled catalytic cycle that made the reaction general, and that is the novel part. I do not think the breadth-of-reach argument alone should rank B035 below B010 or B011, but your own concession that B010 may become acceptable to you once trial status is confirmed is something I will take seriously in my vote.

responses.point: Aili-Daniel prefers B010 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, accepts that no PROTAC is approved, and asks whether Ciulli would be a better third name than Handa or whether the citation should be split.
responses.response: The chair's question is the right one, and I think your trio works against a single citation. Crews and Deshaies conceived heterobifunctional degradation, whereas Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glues. Those are two mechanisms, and a sentence that covers both is likely to be broader than the evidence for either. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands belong with the PROTAC strand. If the expert report shows approved glue-class medicines whose mechanism traces to Handa, a glue-centred or two-strand argument could be defended, but I would not support the current trio on a one-sentence citation without that. I have moved B010 into my alternatives for that reason.

responses.point: Chabes prefers B010 and argues that induced-proximity degraders and the cereblon mechanism share one principle, a small molecule that induces a ternary complex and catalytic removal of the target. He admits that a bundled citation could be criticised as stitching.
responses.response: Your common-principle argument is stronger than the usual framing, because ternary-complex formation is a physical mechanism that can be measured, and I value that. It is also where I would test the citation: do the ternary-complex data for PROTACs and for cereblon-recruited glues actually support one description? If so, the discovery can be stated once. If the glues work through induced surface complementarity found after the fact, the two strands are different. I would want that spelled out in the expert report before I moved B010 above B035, and the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader remains a weakness you have noted yourself.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, prefers B046 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen and accepts that the physiological relevance of in-cell condensates is still contested.
responses.response: I understand the physical appeal, and Sparr's framing of the in vitro thermodynamics as a physical-chemical principle is an easier citation to defend than the claim that condensates organize living cells. My reservation remains the one you list: the committee would be citing a cellular function that the field has not settled. A citation limited to the in vitro framework would be accurate, but it would not be what the opening ballots argued for. The third name also remains unsettled between Rosen, Pappu and Mittag. I would need the report on the field to show a stable consensus on which condensates are functional before I could vote for it.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B011 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman, and told me that B043 is a foundational insight absorbed decades ago and without a clear downstream change in what chemists can do.
responses.response: I accept that point on B043 and I am not asking the committee to rank it above candidacies that changed practice. My own preference is no longer driven by it, which is why B043 is now only my second alternative. On B011, I think restricting the citation to Solexa chemistry is a defensible and tidy choice, and it removes my main attribution worry about mixing lineages. My remaining question is whether the committee regards that as chemistry. If the expert report confirms that the reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry is the decisive step and the 454 and Ju claims are secondary, I could rank B011 close behind B035.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report on organometallic catalysis shows that Kosugi's tin-amide work was catalytic and general enough to require a third name or a changed citation.
Whether the committee regards Pd C-N coupling as sufficiently separate from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether B010 can be described in one accurate sentence covering degraders and cereblon-based glues, and whether the state of clinical trials and approved glue-class drugs supports it this year.
Whether majority support can form for any configuration, given that five distinct first choices remain.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal ground applies to B035. I continue to disclose that my own work on biological energy conversion is scientifically close to B043 and B058, which I now list only as an alternative and not as a preference. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, but her first choice, B002, is outside my field and my vote is not influenced by that tie. No other connection to any credited candidate.
